Sam: Quick sync — saw odd perf when we pushed batch-token-ceil=8192 on a mixed A100/H100 pool. p99 doubled for long contexts. Anyone else?
Anya: Yup I noticed that in the nightly run. p50 fine, but p95/p99 jump on H100 with kv-frag spikes.
Mike: Did kernel selector fall back to the scalar kernel for large combined batches?
Anya: Exactly. Kernel trace shows fallback on H100 for sequences >1024 due to kernel memory estimate mismatch.
Jess: Can you paste the trace?
Anya:
```
[2026-02-01T03:21:12Z] model=redwood-13b kernel=matmul_opt_v2 fit=false reason="workspace_est 12.4GB > avail 11.2GB"\n[2026-02-01T03:21:12Z] fallback=matmul_scalar latency_ms=8.2
```
Sam: That scalar fallback multiplies per-token latency for KV-heavy requests. We need to tighten max tokens-per-batch for H100 when kernel_fit is marginal.
Oliver: What about packing? Are we creating too many mixed-shape batches that trigger worse memory layout?
Anya: Yes — mixed occupancy with large prefix lengths triggers KV fragmentation. Fragmentation shows up as extra memcpy and cache invalidations.
perf-bot: perf-regression-alert: svc=runtime env=staging delta_p99=+120% sample=2026-02-01_03 main_hotpath=kv_cache_write
Mike: For actionables I prototyped a dynamic ceiling: compute token_ceiling = floor(0.9 * kernel_workspace_limit / avg_kv_per_token). Then clamp per-card family. Quick config:
```
{
  "card_class": "H100",
  "base_ceiling": 4096,
  "dynamic_scale": 0.9,
  "min_ceiling": 512,
  "max_ceiling": 6144
}
```
Jess: That seems reasonable. Did you validate throughput tradeoffs?
Mike: Ran microbench: A100 with static 8192 -> raw token/s 1.1M but p99 latency bad. Dynamic -> token/s 0.9M but p99 within SLO. Numbers:
- static 8192 H100: p50 55ms, p95 180ms, p99 420ms, tokens/s 1.05M
- dynamic H100: p50 60ms, p95 90ms, p99 120ms, tokens/s 0.9M
Sam: So small throughput loss but huge SLO improvement. Good trade for enterprise tiers.
Anya: We should encode card-family kernel-fit thresholds into the scheduler so batch formation prefers homogeneous cardsets or bounds mixed batches to lower token ceilings.
Oliver: Also queue policy: when occupancy > 80% throttle token contribution from new requests rather than blocking them. Something like token_budget_target = max(ceil_free_tokens * 0.6, min_ceiling).
Sam: Let's capture concrete proposals: 1) Per-card dynamic ceilings (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100) using kernel_workspace estimates. 2) Scheduler prioritizes same-card grouping for large prefixed requests. 3) Queue policy to dynamically reduce token contribution when occupancy high. 4) Telemetry to emit kernel_fit reasons and KV-frag counters.
Jess: I can add the telemetry: kv_frag_increment, kernel_fit_fail_reason, batch_shape_histogram. Will add tags for card_family and model_size.
perf-bot: perf-note: KV-frag > 3% correlates with p99 spikes in staging (r=0.72).
Sam: Who owns experiments?
Anya: I will own H100 and A100 sweep. Plan: vary base_ceiling in [2048,4096,6144] and dynamic_scale [0.85,0.9,0.95]. I’ll run 4-hour runs with synthetic mixes and live traffic shadowed.
Mike: I’ll do A10/T4/L4 baseline runs and implement scheduler grouping heuristic.
Oliver: I’ll prototype queue token throttler in the admissions controller.
Jess: Target: get telemetry + scheduler + admissions in a canary next week, run overnight sweep.
Sam: One more: kernel selector needs a safe-mode fallback option: if kernel_fit fails due to slight workspace exceed (within 5%) try reduced batch tokens packing before using scalar. That might keep the optimized kernel.
Anya: Good idea. Will add heuristic: try trim_last_request_tokens upto 256 and re-evaluate kernel_fit. If still fails, fall back.
perf-bot: sched-change-sim: predicted p99 reduction ~60% for H100 at 70% occupancy.
infra-bot: deploy-plan scheduled: canary/staging 2026-02-03T02:00Z -> owners: Anya, Mike, Jess.
Sam: OK let's sync tomorrow after initial runs. Thx all :thumbsup:
Mike: adding experiment notes to the tracker and wiring dashboards.
Jess: saved sample telemetry query for KV-frag: `sum(rate(kv_frag_inc[5m])) by (card_family)`
Anya: will post results as screenshots to this thread when runs finish.
Sam: Great. If we see regression on small card families (T4/L4) we'll consider separate min_ceiling profiles.
Oliver: Noted. small-card families often benefit from tighter min_ceiling=256.
Sam: end of thread.
